business_problem: Arcese needed to eliminate long delays in track-and-trace visibility, support forecasting with global real-time data, and avoid staffing a round-the-clock Kafka operations team across its multicloud logistics environment.
solution_summary: Arcese built its next-generation logistics platform around Confluent in Microsoft Azure so transportation and supply-chain events could move in real time across the company's global operations. The streaming architecture connects its transportation management system and related services through Kafka-based communication, using direct database integration with Microsoft SQL Server and access to a large connector ecosystem instead of slow point-to-point exchanges. Because Arcese also operates on Google Cloud Platform, the managed service's multicloud support helps the team keep latency low without creating parallel operations overhead. The platform feeds track-and-trace updates, forecasting inputs, and analytics to customers and internal teams, while freeing developers to focus on new digital logistics services rather than 24/7 cluster administration.

solution_components.name: Confluent
solution_components.role: Runs Arcese's managed streaming platform for global logistics and customer-visibility events.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Azure
solution_components.role: Hosts the Confluent deployment used for Arcese's cloud-native logistics platform.

solution_components.name: Microsoft SQL Server
solution_components.role: Receives and exchanges logistics data through direct Kafka-to-database integration.

data_flow: Transportation and track-and-trace events flow through Confluent in Azure, are connected directly to Microsoft SQL Server and other cloud services, and then feed customer-facing tracking, internal forecasting, and analytics use cases across Arcese's global logistics network.
business_outcome: Arcese reduced track-and-trace latency from nearly an hour to under a minute, improved forecasting and analytics, and gained a scalable managed platform without hiring a large dedicated Kafka team.
